scenes.headline: How an 816B model fits on two Macs
scenes.sub: Meta's Muse Spark Open, read from its file headers.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Gossamer! Muse Spark Open is Meta's new open model, and Meta says it runs on two Mac Studios. Here is how something that big fits on a desk.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Almost every parameter is an expert that sleeps: each token wakes 8 of 256, inside a half-width latent space.
scenes.say: The idea: almost every parameter is an expert that sleeps. Each token wakes only eight of them, and they work in a narrower space.

steps.say: A token arrives at a layer. A router scores every expert and picks eight.
First the token is squeezed to half its width.
Only the chosen experts run, in that narrow space. The rest stay asleep, so each one costs half what it would.
Then the result is projected back to full width and gated into the residual stream.

left.title: Every layer global
left.say: Memory for the context is the other problem. If every layer remembered every token, a million tokens would need over two hundred and sixty gigabytes.

right.title: Three sliding, one global
right.say: Instead, three of every four layers only look back a short window. Just the global layers keep everything, so the whole cache is about sixty-nine gigabytes.

scenes.title: Weight files against two Macs
scenes.note: Two 512 GB Mac Studios hold 1,099.51 GB
scenes.say: Now the bytes. Full precision never fits. The four-bit build fits two Mac Studios with the whole cache and room to spare. That is what the claim means.

steps.say: Unsloth's two-bit files fit a single Mac. Their own chart shows the price: the smaller the file, the further it drifts from the full model.
The two-bit file that fits the smaller Mac drifts more than the one Unsloth recommends for agents.

scenes.text: Sleeping experts and forgetful layers are what put an 816B model on a desk.
scenes.say: So the trick is not magic. Sleeping experts and forgetful layers are what put a model this size on a desk.
Eight experts per token. Short memory in most layers. Four bits on two Macs.
